analysis: The only change in this file is at line 312 of EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift. The test helper recordServerStream now ignores both `.toolCall` and `.toolCallDelta` MLXServerGenerationEvent cases (`case .toolCall, .toolCallDelta: continue`). This is test-only code that uses scripted in-process engine stubs, a fabricated ModelContainer, and no network, weights, or production endpoints. It does not alter any production trust boundary (TB-002, TB-007), key handling (A-003), encryption, or the prefix-cache storage covered by T-041 (SSD tier, cacheSalt scoping, TTL). I did not see the production source for the new `.toolCallDelta` case, so I cannot say how streamed tool-call deltas are handled there. Whether that handling is safe, for example that tool-call content is not leaked or mis-attributed, belongs to the production MLXLMServer change, which is outside these units. Nothing in the visible test file weakens a security assertion. The tests still exercise KV re-slicing, restore-on-throw, the reslice floor refusal, and fail-loud refusal telemetry without exposing secrets. The one thing this test change does is skip assertions on tool-call delta events in the recorded stream. That is a minor coverage gap, not a vulnerability.
